thread:
incidents-bot: PAGED: GPU pool exhaustion detected in us-west-2 — autoscaler not reacting. Pager severity: P1. Paging on-call.

maria: I'm on it — taking page. Initial symptoms: sustained queue growth for inference-service, tokens piling up, 429s and 30s+ tail latencies reported.

leo: seeing high `pendingRequests` on the gpu-pool queue (k8s queue length alert). Metrics ingestion for HPA looks delayed — last adapter scrape ~10m ago.

ajay: confirmed. Prometheus scrape for gpu-metrics-exporter stalled, prometheus-adapter reports error: `500 downstream timeout`. HPA hasn't seen updated custom metrics.

maria: quick customer impact check — two mid-market customers reporting degraded throughput (customer A and B), non-blocking but high token billing. Not fully degraded but some calls error with 429.

sam: can we manual-scale Dedicated GPU pool while root cause is investigated? We have reserved capacity headroom.

maria: yes -- plan: 1) manual scale up GPU pool by +20% to buy time, 2) investigate prometheus-adapter and metrics-server, 3) fallback HPA to CPU metric temporarily, 4) drain long-running requests if needed.

tina: I'm doing a quick healthcheck. `kubectl get pods -n infra prometheus-adapter -o wide` shows adapter in CrashLoopBackOff intermittently on node ip-10-0-3-5.

leo: logs from adapter: ```
E0321 17:03:12.456 prom_adapter.go:212] failed to read remote write: read tcp 10.0.0.8:443: i/o timeout
E0321 17:03:18.129 prom_adapter.go:212] failed to convert metrics: unexpected EOF
```

ajay: also seeing kubelet churn on that node around same time. Could be network blipping to metrics backend. Any recent infra deploys?

maria: no scheduled infra deploys in last hour. Network team, can you confirm if there was a vpc route flapping or control-plane change? @networking-team? (mentioning externally)

sam: meanwhile I'll run the mitigation commands to scale the GPU pool and HPA fallback. Executing: ```
# scale Dedicated GPU pool
redwoodctl capacity set --pool gpu-usw2 --percent 120
# patch HPA to fallback to CPU target while custom metrics backfill
kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/metrics","value":[{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","target":{"type":"Utilization","averageUtilization":65}}}]}]'
```

maria: good. I've alerted support to set an outbound status: brief note that a performance degradation is affecting high-throughput customers and we're actively mitigating.

tina: I restarted prometheus-adapter on node ip-10-0-3-5 and cordoned the node to prevent additional pods being scheduled until we verify stability. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter -n infra` done.

leo: after restart, adapter started accepting scrapes but still lagging. Prometheus shows backlog of ~4m samples to process; adapter latency reduced from 1m to ~12s. HPA custom metric still not updated due to scrape interval + backlog.

ajay: I'm patching HPA status to force an immediate reconciliation once samples arrive, and adding a temporary horizontalpodautoscaler override to minReplicas=6 to reduce queue. Running: ```
kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa -n prod --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}' --type=merge
```

maria: manual pool scale completed, HPA patched to CPU-only fallback and minReplicas bumped. Queue growth stopped shortly after — pendingRequests trending down. Some in-flight requests still long.

sam: customer impact update: 6% of requests hit 429s during peak, majority now recovered. Support posted interim update.

tina: investigating root cause: prometheus remote-write endpoint had a transient TLS handshake error with remote storage (logs show `tls: handshake failure`) leading to adapter timeouts. Working with metrics vendor to confirm.

leo: also noticing `metrics-server` had restarted on 2 nodes; kube-system events show `OOMKilled` for metrics-server pod due to spike in scrape throughput while backlog was processed. Might explain additional flakiness for HPA.

ajay: mitigation: increased metrics-server memory to 1.5Gi and rolled. Patch: ```
kubectl set resources deployment metrics-server -n kube-system --limits=memory=1500Mi --requests=memory=800Mi
kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-server -n kube-system
```

maria: good. Next steps: 1) keep manual capacity +20% for 30m while we validate, 2) monitor adapter backlog until < 30s lag, 3) revert HPA fallback once custom metrics resume and are stable for 5m, 4) follow up with vendor on TLS handshake root cause.

sam: I've set a 1h scheduled rollback: if adapter backlog clears and HPA sees metrics consistently for 5m, we'll revert minReplicas and restore custom metrics.

tina: leaving cordon on node ip-10-0-3-5 until network team confirms no further packet loss.

maria: handoff — I'm paged through but need to step out for 25m. Taking initial mitigation done, handing to ajay for active monitoring and vendor escalation. @ajay you're next.

ajay: taking it. I'll be primary for the next 45m. I'll keep channel updated every 10m or on notable changes.

leo: added runbook note: `prom-adapter-backpressure` with steps we ran (scale pool, restart adapter, patch HPA, increase metrics-server mem). Will follow up with a postmortem template after incident closes.

maria: final impact summary for timeline note: outage start 5287654321, manual mitigations applied 5287654390, traffic recovered to normal by 5287654560. Root cause probable: transient TLS handshake failures to remote-metrics storage causing adapter timeouts -> backlog -> metrics-server OOM -> delayed HPA reaction -> GPU queue growth and partial throttling.

ajay: confirmed, marking as live-mitigated. Creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-infra for RCA and vendor coordination.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status=mitigated, mitigation_time=5287654560, assignee=eng-infra.

maria: thanks team. I'll add customer-facing notes and coordinate postmortem scheduling.

ajay: I'll keep watch until handoff to next oncall.

tina: leaving logs and commands used in the incident thread gist: https://internal.gists/reviews/abc123 (internal link).

maria: end of thread for now — we'll follow up in the postmortem channel. :thumbsup:
